newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Lend Lease pleased with profit, but brokers unsure.
newsitem.headline: Lend Lease pleased with profit, but brokers unsure.

text.p: Property and financial services group Lend Lease Corp Ltd on Friday became one of the few Australian bluechips to achieve higher profits in 1995/96.
The group also forecast even better times ahead as costs are cut and overseas projects near completion.

Brokers and analysts, however, were less than impressed by the 7.6 percent rise in 1995/96 (July-June) net profit to A$280 million (US$222 million) and instead fussed about how the company achieved its growth in the year just gone.
"In our view it was a bit of a disappointing number," said the head trader of a European-owned broking house.
"We were going for a slightly higher profit, especially as the tax rate was so low," he said, referring to a more than threefold cut in the tax bill to A$9.6 million.
Shares in Lend Lease tracked the rest of the sharemarket lower on Friday, ending 43 cents down at A$20.55.
The result was in the middle of analysts expectations.

But it compared favourably with other top 20 Australian firms such as mining, steel and petroleum giant Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd, building products group Boral, sugar producer and builder CSR Ltd and paper maker Amcor Ltd which have all blamed the poor economy for weak annual profits.
"This is not an extraordinary result in any way," one analyst said. "But given that companies like Boral are down 30 percent maybe a flat profit is very acceptable."
As expected, Lend Lease's profit was underpinned by its MLC insurance and funds management arm, and helped by larger dividend payments from its investment in Westpac Banking Corp.
Lend Lease now has a direct three percent stake in Westpac after selling a six percent holding through a warrant issue earlier in the year.

"Lend Lease has delivered a profit of A$280 million in an Australian environment of low growth and low inflation and that is despite a once-off provision (of A$57 million) for two shopping centres in Victoria," managing director David Higgins said.

He said net profit would rise further in 1996/97 and by the year 2000 he expected to achieve double digit rises in sales and net profits from the financial services division, mainly due to a planned 40 percent cut in costs.

Higgins could not make a specific prediction on the profit increase expected from the property division, which includes project management and development in Australia, Asia, Britain and the United States.
"We will be making more investments in the next few months in Asia and the UK. We will be deploying our capital where we find the right opportunities," he said.
Higgins said the company would decide in the next month or so on further property investments in Jakarta, Bangkok and Britain.
Lend Lease is the driving force behind the A$1.2 billion Bluewater Shopping Centre in Kent which is due to open in 1999 and which already is 50 percent leased. (A$1=79.4 U.S. cents)
